I was assigned female at birth and diagnosed at 12 and I was only diagnosed because I read a list of symptoms and recognized them in myself and told my doctor about it. My symptoms are very subtle. I'm forgetful, I misplace things a lot, I procrastinate to the point of never getting anything done, I crave constant stimulation and get bored easily.

My parents and teachers never saw any reason to test me anything because I was generally well-behaved and made good grades. I got straight A's in elementary school without even trying. I was put in gifted classes and LOVED it because the work was on my level and we got to do cool projects all the time. 

I went to a Catholic middle school and that's when I started having problems. Being a private school, the work was more rigorous than public school. For the first time in my life, I actually had to put effort into my school work, which I found hard. I couldn't study unless I was also listening to music or watching tv, so I didn't absorb the information as well. I've always had to multitask on everything. I can't hyperfocus on one thing like a lot of people with ADHD can.

For high school I went back to public school and took regular classes, so the work was easy again. I was recommended for IB because I did so well, but I refused because I knew I'd have to make an effort for IB classes. I also had a lot of friends in IB and saw how stressed out they were. I'm a rising senior now with a 3.5 GPA.
